property_summary: Once the contract is Initialized, any call to SetMinSum must revert without changing MinSum; the mutant performs the assignment before the check, so a reverted SetMinSum(_val) still leaves MinSum == _val in M but not in P.

For any fuzzed value v and any fuzzed choice of whether the contract has been Initialized(), SetMinSum(v) must revert exactly when the contract is already initialized and, when it reverts, must leave MinSum unchanged; the mutant assigns MinSum even on the reverting path, so a reverted call leaves M.MinSum()==v while P.MinSum() keeps its old value.

For any fuzzed value v, a call to SetMinSum(v) succeeds exactly when the contract is not yet initialized and then sets MinSum to v; when the contract is already initialized the call must revert and leave MinSum at its previous value — the mutant assigns MinSum even on the reverting path, so a reverted SetMinSum leaves MinSum == v instead of the prior value.

property_summary: Once Initialized() has been called, any SetMinSum(_val) must revert and leave MinSum unchanged; the mutant assigns MinSum before the check, so a reverted SetMinSum leaves MinSum == _val instead of the prior value.

For every fuzzed value v, a call to SetMinSum(v) must either succeed (only possible before initialization) and leave MinSum == v, or revert and leave MinSum unchanged; the mutant assigns MinSum before the initialization check, so a SetMinSum call on an initialized contract updates MinSum to v even though it reverts.

Once C is initialized via Initialized(), calling SetMinSum must never change MinSum; the mutant drops the guard so a post-initialization SetMinSum(val) makes c.MinSum() equal val, breaking the invariant.
